payload.name: Retrieve alternate focus areas for 'besides' questions
payload.description: When a question asks what someone has been focusing on lately besides an explicit main activity (e.g., studying, work), search for other life domains such as relationships, hobbies, and social activities.
content: When a question asks what someone has been focusing on lately besides an explicit main activity (e.g., studying, work), do not stop at generic self-care or non-study queries; add targeted searches for relationship and hobby terms like 'partner', 'relationship', 'together', 'hobby', and 'activity'.
Include event and preference memory kinds in these searches, and inspect memories that mention the person alongside another name or a joint activity even if they do not literally contain 'focus'.
Stop after two or three distinct query attempts once a plausible non-primary focus area is found; answer only from visible evidence.

solves: When a question asks what someone has been focusing on lately besides a primary activity (e.g., studying or work), retrieval can miss relationship and hobby memories if queries are anchored only to the negated activity. This skill guides complementary searches across other life domains.
